chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinani, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) when an old man entered upon him and said, 'O Abu Abdullah! I complain to you about my children and their ingratitude, and my brothers and their disloyalty during my old age.'

So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'O man! Indeed, for the Truth there is a dominion (era/condition), and for falsehood there is a dominion, and each one of these two is humiliated in the dominion of its counterpart.'
And the least of what befalls the believer in the dominion of falsehood is ingratitude from his children and disloyalty from his brothers.
And no believer attains anything of prosperity in the dominion of falsehood except that he is tried before his death, either in his body, or in his children, or in his wealth.
Until Allah purifies him from what he earned in the dominion of falsehood and completes his share in the dominion of the Truth.
So be patient and receive glad tidings.

key_terms.جَفَاء: Disloyalty, coldness, or estrangement, often from relatives or brothers.
key_terms.دَوْلَة: Dominion, era, or condition; referring to a period of divine decree or worldly state.
key_terms.رَفَاهِيَة: Prosperity, comfort, or ease in worldly life.
key_terms.عُقُوق: Ingratitude or disobedience, specifically of children towards parents.
key_terms.يُخَلِّصَهُ: He purifies him or delivers him (from sins through trials).

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual wisdom behind family ingratitude and trials in old age according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) contextualizes familial ingratitude not merely as a social grievance but as a divine mechanism of purification (*kaffarah*) during the 'dominion of falsehood' (*dawlat al-batil*). This scholarly interpretation highlights the Shia concept of *sabr* (patient endurance) as an active spiritual practice that accelerates the believer's transition to the 'dominion of truth' (*dawlat al-haqq*), ensuring their sins are expiated before death.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany who said,

‘I was in the Presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> when an old man came over to him<sup>asws</sup> and he said, ‘O Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>! I complain to you<sup>asws</sup> of my children and their ingratitude, and of my brothers and their disloyalty during my old age’.
So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O you! For the truth there is a nation and for the falsehood there is a nation, and every one of these two is disgraced in the nation of its counterpart.
And that the least of what the Momin would attain in the nation of the falsehood is the ingratitude of his children and the disloyalty from his brothers;

and there is none from a Momin attaining anything from the prosperity in the nation of the falsehood except that he would be Tried, before his death, either (by an illness) in his body, and either regarding his child, and either regarding his wealth (losses)
until Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Purifies him from what he had earned in the nation of the falsehood, and Set aside his share for him in the nation of the truth.
Therefore be patient and receive glad tidings’.
en.sarwar: 12. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinani who has said the following:

“Once I was in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) that an old man came and said, ‘O abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) I complain to you against my sons for their failing to maintain good relations with parents and against my brothers for their injustice to me during my old age.’
Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) said, ‘O you, for truth there is a kingdom and for falsehood there is a kingdom. Each of them is humiliated in the kingdom of the other.
The least that a believer may suffer in the kingdom of falsehood is the failure of his children to maintain good relations with parents, and injustice from his brothers.
Any believer who may receive comfort in the kingdom of falsehood, for this he faces suffering before his death, either in his physical health, his children or his property
until Allah purifies him from what he has received in the kingdom of falsehood and will expand his share in the kingdom of truth.
